notes.title: Chorus of Carcosa - Movement & Stamina Update
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

The first weekend for Chorus of Carcosa was huge, and we’ve gathered a ton of valuable feedback.
Thanks to all our players! We’re actively working on the game, and today, we’ve got a big update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039697/c507964a589ab01eca386287f58ced77c852fb24.jpg[/img]

[b]Today's update focuses on the following issues:[/b]

[list]
[*] Full character movement rebalance: the character now walks and crawls faster, and can run for a longer duration
[*] Stamina and breath indicators are now displayed on the screen. It will disappear when indicators are full to avoid unnecessary clutter
[*] Added more shortcuts in The Winter Garden to make dodging the monster easier
[*] The screen darkening during breath-holding will no longer obstruct visibility
[*] Fixed a fatality bug that occasionally caused the scene to be viewed from the side
[*] Added a prompt about crouching during the first monster encounter
[*] Updated button visuals for skipping the credits
[*] Added some visual hints for star map and musical staff puzzles
[*] And a batch of minor fixes 
[/list]
[i][b]KNOWN ISSUES:[/b][/i] you can encounter a bug - when you die with this stat on the screen, it will break until the next level is loaded. 
We are already working on fixing this bug.

We're carefully reading all the comments about your experience. So if you encounter any bugs or want to share your feedback - feel free to [url=https://discord.com/invite/b7ZjxM5FGb]join our Discord[/url] or write in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2987750/discussions/]Steam Discussions[/url].

notes.title: Developer Diary - The Idea
notes.content:
[h2]Hey everyone!
[/h2]

In these updates, we’ll talk about our ideas we’ve used while making the game. We’ll also include some concept art and work-in-progress stuff to show you how everything is coming together.

[b]Chameleon 42 has been a reliable partner in creating video games for many studios for years.[/b] We specialize in game art of different complexity. At the end of 2023, we decided to create something of our own. After researching different genres and exploring lots of ideas for our first game, [b]we chose psychological horror[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039697/4557adf5a4cebe5493a46f0601e3992777aa2cc3.png[/img]

The main source of inspiration is quite obvious—it’s Robert W. Chambers’ collection of stories, The King in Yellow. While working on Carcosa (the reverse side of reality), we often looked to the original Silent Hill tetralogy for guidance (there have been countless hot debates within the team about which game in the franchise is the best). 

The team has absorbed so much diverse content in the horror genre—from games and movies to anime and literature—that it feels like we’ve created a kind of collective subconscious where ideas are born.
Also, we have a deep love for H.P. Lovecraft’s work and its rich mythos. However, once the overall concept of the game and the themes we wanted to explore came together, [b]we immediately knew that The King in Yellow would be the perfect foundation.[/b] 

The thin line between reality and madness, and the creeping dread of the unknown aligns perfectly with the atmosphere we wanted to create. Additionally, The King in Yellow explores a lesser-known corner of horror, giving us the opportunity to create something unique while staying true to the broader Lovecraftian theme.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039697/207587f441964db4d4da00e69c5b4e375b8a9029.png[/img][i]*Early concept of apartments[/i]

But what kind of experience do we want the player to have? In the early chapters, [b]we focused on the protagonist’s growing anxiety[/b]. Some team members know firsthand what it’s like to live with this kind of feeling, having dealt with it their entire lives. We’ve tried to portray this feeling as authentically as possible (within the limits of the universe we’ve chosen). 

When something as simple as stepping out to pick up a package can feel like a trial. When a slightly open door is more terrifying than monstrous creatures. When a knock at the door can completely throw you off balance. 

Above all, [b]we aim to create an atmospheric horror experience that tells an engaging story[/b]. The short 2-3 hours format allows us to keep the game packed with action and free of unnecessary fillers.

And beyond that… Well, it’s hard to avoid spoilers! If you’d like to learn more about the game, follow us on social media and stay tuned for upcoming posts.

🟡[url=https://x.com/ChorusOfCarcosa]Twitter[/url]
🟡[url=https://discord.com/invite/b7ZjxM5FGb]Discord[/url]

Thanks for reading,
Chameleon 42

notes.title: The Chorus of Carcosa Playtest Has Ended!
notes.content:
The gates of [b]Carcosa[/b] have closed - for now. 

We want to extend a huge thank you to everyone who braved the nightmare and participated in the playtest. Your courage, feedback, and support have been nothing short of incredible!

[b]Playtest Highlights:[/b]
[list]
[*] Over [b]1200 brave souls[/b] requested access to the playtest.
[*] We gathered [b]~1500 wishlists[/b] on Steam!
[*] Your feedback has been invaluable, and we've already begun working on it.
[/list]
But most importantly, we were blown away by all the support from our amazing community. We’re grateful to every single one of you. Your enthusiasm is what keeps us going!

Stay tuned for more updates as we continue to polish and expand this journey into madness. The [b]echoes of Carcosa[/b] will call again soon...

Thank you for being a part of this nightmare. Your support means everything to us!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2987750/Chorus_of_Carcosa/
